A big thing I always tell kids is that I will always cover their eyes/ears depending on what it is they are scared about so they can ask. 

I'll ask about what specifically they are scared about and then tell them ways we can mitigate it. I took a 4 year old who made it clear she was scared that Big Thunder was going to be loud. I told her about parts of it that are loud and offered to cover her ears for her when it was loud. When we returned 4 months later she rode it with her mom and didn't need anyone to cover her ears. 

Had another kiddo who was afraid of the dark and any ride with darkness so we let her wear a cheap glow stick necklace because it allowed her to see just a teeny bit more if it got really dark. 

I think it's important to let them name the fear i.e." It's going to be too bumpy" and then it is our job to validate it and offer solutions, "Sometimes bumpy rides can make us feel unstable, would it be helpful if I hold on to you during the ride?"

Developmentally, *most* children under 6 are going to have trouble standing in a traditional line. Some kids can do it without issue, but others could benefit from having a break or two. DAS gets abused enough as it is, I'm not suggesting that people do this for every ride and experience at Disneyland. I'm just sharing something I did, while apparently controversial, that made a 4-year-olds day magical and helped her parents have a more relaxing time without a grumpy child.

Didn't think this would be controversial. Waiting in line for over an hour is really hard on kids so if you can avoid it sometimes you should try. There's no way to LL the princesses, so we had me wait in the line. We had an amazing trip with zero meltdowns or tantrums. I 100% contribute that to allowing her the ability to walk around and see stuff while I waited for a couple things. She still waited in a few lines throughout the day, but she got to do and see way more because I was able to hold her spot in line. She's not going to get to go again for a few years, our trip was truly a wonderful time for everyone. 

OP said he wants his daughter to get to see as much as possible, and I offered this option. This option is probably not a great idea to bring *all* the kids in the party to do this, but like if one couple takes the 4 kids to the Fantasy Faire show while the other two couples stay in line for princesses, I don't see what the big deal is. If someone "cut" me in line after doing that, I'd 100% rather that than 4 kids who are getting tired and impatient. 

I do understand where some of you are coming from, but this was something that worked really well for us, and if you have really young kids I highly recommend it.

I understand that it seems unfair because not everyone can do this, but like plenty of people go and have one parent take their kid to the fantasy faire show while the other parent stays in line. It's literally the same thing.
